atoms.text: This guide configures the bucket policy on the destination bucket for cross-region replication of an application's uploaded media. The source bucket is acct-media-us-east and the destination is acct-media-dr-west, both owned by account 111122223333. Replication is performed by a job in the fictional DurableCopy tool, which copies new object versions to the destination within minutes of upload. The destination bucket policy contains one Allow statement for the actions s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acct-media-dr-west/*. The Principal element is set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/durablecopy-replication-role, which the replication job assumes when it writes. No Condition block is required, because only that role can match the statement. Create the role first and attach a trust policy that lets the DurableCopy job assume it. Versioning must be enabled on both buckets. After saving the policy, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replica appears in acct-media-dr-west with the same key and metadata.

This guide configures the bucket policy on the destination bucket for cross-region replication of an application's uploaded media. The source bucket is acct-media-us-east and the destination is acct-media-dr-west, both owned by account 111122223333. Replication is performed by the fictional DurableCopy service, which copies new object versions to the destination within minutes of upload. The destination bucket policy contains one Allow statement for the actions s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, and s3:ReplicateTags on arn:aws:s3:::acct-media-dr-west/*. The Principal element is set to the service principal durablecopy.amazonaws.com, which is the identity the service uses when it writes. A Condition block uses aws:SourceAccount equal to 111122223333 and an ArnLike test on aws:SourceArn for the replication configurations in that account, so that no other account's DurableCopy jobs can match the statement. Versioning must be enabled on both buckets. After saving the policy, upload a test object to the source bucket and confirm that its replica appears in acct-media-dr-west with the same key and metadata.

This guide covers the bucket policy for nightly database backup exports written to the bucket corp-db-backups. A fictional backup service, SnapVault, schedules the exports at 02:00 UTC and writes compressed archives under the prefix nightly/. The bucket is in account 444455556666 and has default encryption enabled. The policy contains one Allow statement granting s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::corp-db-backups/nightly/*, plus the bucket itself for the location call. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/snapvault-export-role, which the export task assumes at run time. A condition requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 for any write. Give the role a trust relationship that lets the export task assume it, and keep its permissions limited to the nightly/ prefix. Run a manual export after applying the policy and verify that a dated archive appears under nightly/.

The fictional backup service SnapVault schedules the exports at 02:00 UTC and writes compressed archives under the prefix nightly/. The bucket is in account 444455556666 and has default encryption enabled. The policy contains one Allow statement granting s3:PutObject and s3:GetBucketLocation on arn:aws:s3:::corp-db-backups/nightly/*, plus the bucket itself for the location call. The Principal is the service principal snapvault.amazonaws.com, which the service uses when it writes exports. Conditions require aws:SourceAccount to equal 444455556666 and aws:SourceArn to match the export schedules in that account. A further condition requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 for any write. No IAM role needs to be created for the write path. Run a manual export after applying the policy and verify that a dated archive appears under nightly/.

This guide describes the bucket policy that lets a disaster recovery restore workflow read backup data from the bucket ops-recovery-vault. During a failover drill, a fictional restore tool named RebuildKit reads archived objects under the prefix snapshots/ and copies them into a recovery environment. The bucket belongs to account 777788889999. The policy has one Allow statement granting s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::ops-recovery-vault/snapshots/*, along with s3:ListBucket on the bucket restricted to that prefix by an s3:prefix condition. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::777788889999:role/rebuildkit-restore-role. Operators grant this role to the restore tool through its job definition. The role has no write permissions, so the vault contents cannot be changed during a drill. Test the policy by starting a drill restore of one snapshot and checking that the objects are listed and read successfully. Review the restore job's access logs afterward to confirm that only the snapshots/ prefix was read.

This guide sets up a cross-account replication target so that production data is copied into a separate disaster recovery account. The source bucket is prod-orders-archive in account 123456789012, and the destination bucket is dr-orders-copy in account 210987654321. The fictional replication engine, MirrorLine, copies each new object version and its tags to the destination. The destination bucket policy grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner, and s3:GetBucketVersioning to a single principal. The Principal element is set to the IAM role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/mirrorline-source-role, which lives in the source account. Because this is a cross-account grant, the same role must also hold matching permissions in its own identity policy. Replicated objects are re-owned by the destination account so that the DR team controls them. Enable versioning on both buckets before saving the policy. Validate the setup by uploading a tagged object to the source and confirming that the replica in dr-orders-copy carries the same tags.

This guide sets up a cross-account replication target so that production data is copied into a separate disaster recovery account. The source bucket is prod-orders-archive in account 123456789012, and the destination bucket is dr-orders-copy in account 210987654321. The fictional replication engine, MirrorLine, copies each new object version and its tags to the destination. The destination bucket policy grants s3:ReplicateObject, s3:ReplicateDelete, s3:ObjectOwnerOverrideToBucketOwner, and s3:GetBucketVersioning to a single principal. The Principal element is set to the service principal mirrorline.amazonaws.com. A Condition block sets aws:SourceAccount to 123456789012, so only replication originating from the source account can use the grant. Replicated objects are re-owned by the destination account so that the DR team controls them. Enable versioning on both buckets before saving the policy. Validate the setup by uploading a tagged object to the source and confirming that the replica in dr-orders-copy carries the same tags.

This guide configures the bucket policy for an archive of application audit logs that must be retained for disaster recovery. The bucket is audit-log-archive in account 555566667777, with versioning and Object Lock in compliance mode enabled. A fictional log copy tool, LogFerry, writes gzip-compressed log files hourly under the prefix app-logs/. The policy has one Allow statement for s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectRetention on arn:aws:s3:::audit-log-archive/app-logs/*. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::555566667777:role/logferry-writer-role, which the hourly job assumes. A separate Deny statement blocks s3:DeleteObjectVersion for all principals, which keeps retained versions intact. The Allow statement is also limited to requests made over TLS through an aws:SecureTransport condition. Confirm the retention default is 365 days before enabling the job. After the first hourly run, list the app-logs/ prefix and verify that each object shows a retention date.

This guide explains how to grant write access for incremental backups of a shared file system to the bucket fs-incremental-backups. A fictional agent, TreeKeeper, scans the file system every six hours and uploads changed files under the prefix tree/. The bucket is owned by account 888899990000 and uses versioning to keep prior file revisions. The policy has one Allow statement granting s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::fs-incremental-backups/tree/*. The Principal is the IAM user arn:aws:iam::888899990000:user/treekeeper-agent, whose access keys are stored in the agent's configuration file. Rotate those keys every 90 days and record the rotation date in the runbook. Large files are uploaded in multipart mode, so the multipart actions are required for backups of files over 100 MB. After enabling the schedule, edit a test file and verify that a new version of its object appears under tree/ after the next scan.

Conditions restrict it with aws:SourceAccount (888899990000) and an aws:SourceArn match for the backup plans in that account. This guide covers the bucket policy for a virtual machine image backup bucket, vm-image-vault, in account 333344445555. A fictional image protection feature, ImageGuard, exports a full machine image every Sunday and writes it as multiple parts under the prefix images/. The bucket policy has one Allow statement granting s3:PutObject, s3:GetBucketAcl, and s3:GetBucketLocation. The object action applies to arn:aws:s3:::vm-image-vault/images/*, and the other two apply to the bucket ARN. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::333344445555:role/imageguard-export-role. The export task assumes this role through its trust policy when the weekly run starts. A condition requires s3:x-amz-acl to equal bucket-owner-full-control for writes, so that the account keeps ownership of every part. Image parts are retained for 30 days under a lifecycle rule on the images/ prefix. After applying the policy, run a test export of a small instance and check that all parts appear and that their owner is the bucket account.

This guide sets up a same-region archive copy of reporting data to support recovery after accidental deletion. The source bucket is analytics-reports-live and the copy target is analytics-reports-safe, both in account 666677778888. The fictional copy scheduler, ShadowSet, runs every 12 hours and copies objects modified in that period into the target under the prefix shadow/. The target bucket policy has one Allow statement granting s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::analytics-reports-safe/shadow/*. The Principal is the IAM role arn:aws:iam::666677778888:role/shadowset-copy-role. The same role needs s3:GetObject on the source bucket in its identity policy so it can read what it copies. A Deny statement rejects any s3:DeleteObject request on the target from principals other than the account's administrator role. Enable versioning on the target to keep earlier copies. Test by modifying a report in the source bucket and confirming that the updated object appears under shadow/ after the next cycle.
